agent: saved-battle wave, reader B (bombings, finished battles, sunk ships)
question: The three bombing kinds, the list of finished battles and the top-level sunk_ships block, as a save holds them and as a load takes them back.

addresses.name: CBomberCombatant::SaveContents
addresses.comment: **Slot 2 of CBomberCombatant: the bombers' side of a bombing in a save.** CCombatant::SaveContents (0x165010) first - `dice`, one `unit` id pair per unit, one `sunk_ship` id pair per ship on the side's sunk list, `losses`, `size`, `tactic` where set (never on a bombing) - then its own four keys in this order: `strength` = +0x10E4 as a thousandths fixed point (text saves through MakeFixedToken, binary ones as a `%d` int token), then `building` (+0x10B4), `pool` (+0x10C4) and `current_producing` (+0x10D4), each through SaveWriteFixedVector (rva 0xC8050), which writes `key=`, a block, every element as a fixed point followed by one space at column 0, and the closing brace on the last value's line; nothing at all for an empty vector. So `building` has one figure per building of the database (index 0 the built-in nobuilding, then common/buildings.txt in file order - 12 in Their Finest Hour) and `pool` and `current_producing` seven, in the goods order supplies, fuel, money, crude oil, metal, energy, rare materials. Unconditional: every bomber side writes all four. 0x55FE90 to the `ret 4` at 0x55FF3D. The struct record's +0x10E4 comment called this 'the getter at 0x15FE90'. Read back by CBomberCombatant::LoadKey (0x15FDF0).
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing: call 0x565010, then SaveWriteKey with ecx = 0x259 (strength), 0x1FE (building), 0x484 (pool), 0x485 (current_producing) per ghidra/saveTokens.json, the last three through 0x4C8050 with lea [ebx+0x10B4/0x10C4/0x10D4]. vtable.py --all puts 0x55FE90 at slot 2 of CBomberCombatant and only there (CCombatant's slot 2 is 0x565010). Agrees key for key and figure count for figure count with the five bomber blocks in Germany1936_09_02_21, Ireland1936_02_02_04, Ireland1938_06_03_03 and Ireland1938_08_03_14 (three). Would be wrong if a save showed a bomber side without one of the four keys, or the keys in another order.

addresses.name: CBomberCombatant::ReportBombingEnd
addresses.comment: **Slot 10 of CBomberCombatant, which CCombat::End calls on both sides when a bombing ends: the end-of-bombing report, which is why the four tallies are saved.** Nothing where the combat is a convoy raid's (+0x2B), or the side has no country (+0x5C) or no unit (+0x48). Otherwise it builds messages with PROV, ATTACKER, ATTACKER_ADJ and ORDER, and a line for each building whose figure in `buildings_destroyed` (+0x10B4, walked over the building database's length) is not nought (BOMB_DAMAGE_BUILDING, NAME, SIZE), for each of the seven goods taken from the stockpile (+0x10C4, BOMB_DAMAGE_STOCKPILE) and from production (+0x10D4, BOMB_DAMAGE_PRODUCTION); it then sets `strength_damage_dealt` (+0x10E4) to itself x k_thousandths_10_combat (10) / 1000 and, where that is not nought and a condition on the other side not read holds, a BOMB_DAMAGE_MEN line; a BOMB_SINK_SHIP line per ship on its sunk list (+0x28, count +0x30), BOMB_DAMAGING_SHIPS, DAMAGE/DAMAGE_SHORT; and the message keys BOMBENDTHEM and BOMBENDUS. Near its end, for every sub unit of the side's units whose type's byte +0x33 is set, RemoveRegimentFromUnit and CGameState::DisposeSubUnit (0x55FC91) - what that byte is was not read. 0x55E030 to the bare `ret` at 0x55FDEC, 0x1DC0 bytes: only its strings, its reads of +0x10B4..+0x10E4 and the disposal loop were read; the name is ours.
addresses.evidence: vtable.py --all CCombatant CBomberCombatant: slot 10 is 0x55E030 for CBomberCombatant and the 1691-holder stub 0xABF890 for CCombatant and the three target combatants. The string pushes (BOMBENDTHEM at 0x55F8BD, BOMBENDUS at 0x55FA79, the BOMB_DAMAGE_* keys) and the ten reads of +0x10B4/+0x10C4/+0x10D4/+0x10E4 are in the listing. Likely, because the message keys say what it is; would be wrong if CCombat::End (0x17AB00) were found not to call slot 10, or if the strings belonged to a function abutting inside this extent (retsBefore from 0x55E030 to 0x55FDEC shows only the final ret in the listing grep).

addresses.name: CCombatManager_LoadKey_GroundBombingController
addresses.comment: **What a load rebuilds of a ground bombing that the save does not hold: the bombed side's country.** In CCombatManager::LoadKey's `ground_bombing` arm, after the combat is made (0x2FE20), linked (CCombatManager::AddCombat), given its combatants (slot 6) and loaded (slot 3, which ends in CCombat::AttachAndRegister): a 0x14-byte node {the province's controller tag +0x334, its id +0x338, prev, next 0, byte 0} is appended to the defender's `countries` list (CCombatant +0x54 first, +0x58 last, +0x5C count) - **not** to `own_countries` (+0x64). It is the same thing CCombatManager::CreateCombat does for a kind 4 at 0x431444, so a loaded ground bombing names its defender as a new one does: the controller as the province block of the save has it, since provinces precede `combat`. The `land_bombing` and `naval_bombing` arms do nothing after the load: their defenders' countries come back through the `unit` keys (CCombatant::AddUnit). Neither list is in a save.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x42FDB4..0x42FE0F: mov esi,[edi+0x18] (the province), mov edi,[edi+0x14] (the defender), operator new(0x14), [eax]=[esi+0x334], [eax+4]=[esi+0x338], linked through +0x58/+0x5C/+0x54. The arm is reached only on token 0x523 (sub eax,0x523; je 0x42FD7D). CreateCombat's kind-4 block at 0x431444..0x431493 is the same shape. Wrong if CCombat::LoadKey or AttachAndRegister already put the controller there, which would make the list hold it twice - neither touches +0x54 by the record.

addresses.name: CGameState_LoadKey_SunkShipsArm
addresses.comment: **How a load takes the top-level `sunk_ships` block back.** CGameState::LoadKey's arm for token 0x59F reads the block with its own loop (so the block itself gets no AfterLoad): until `}` or the end of the file, each key is a country's tag - looked up by CCountryDataBase::GetTag on the key's text, `---` with id 0 where it is none - and its value a ship: a fresh CShip (operator new 0xF8, CShip::CShip at 0x1ADB60) is appended to the game state's sunk list (+0x20 first, +0x24 last, +0x28 count, 0x10-byte nodes {ship, prev, next, byte}), given the tag as its owner (CSubUnit +0x94/+0x98) **before** it is loaded, and loaded through its slot 3 - CShip::LoadKey (`air`) over CSubUnit::LoadKey, and CSubUnit's AfterLoad, which registers the ship's saved id (and raises the unit counter past it) or mints one. So a sunk ship's owner comes from its key and nothing else, the list keeps the file's order, and every ship is in the id registry before `combat` is read - which is what lets a combatant's `sunk_ship` key find it.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x6802E2..0x68044A: the token switch reaches it by sub eax,0x585; sub eax,0x1A (0x59F, `sunk_ships` in saveTokens.json); peek/compare against tokens 4 and 0x13; 0x518480 (CCountryDataBase::GetTag) on parse+0x24; push 0xF8 / call 0x5ADB60; node {edi, [ebx+0x24], 0, 0}; [edi+0x94]/[edi+0x98] stored, then call [vtable+0xC]. Checked against all 33 saves: 7 hold entries (2 to 30), every entry `<TAG>={ id name type organisation strength highest experience [sunk_by] [pride] <technologies> }`. Wrong if an entry's owner differed from its key in a save - nothing writes the owner inside the block.

addresses.name: CGameState_SaveContents_SunkShips
addresses.comment: **How the top-level `sunk_ships` block is written**, inside CGameState::SaveContents after the countries: SaveWriteKey(0x59F) and a block, **always - an empty list gives `sunk_ships={ }`**; then for each node of the game state's sunk list (+0x20, through node +8), in list order, SaveWriteNamedObject with the ship's owner tag (CSubUnit +0x94) as the key and the ship as the object - CShip::SaveContents, i.e. CSubUnit's keys and `air` per air group on its list (+0xDC), which a sunk carrier never has because CGameState::DisposeSubUnit took its groups off before putting it on the list. The block is closed with the writer's depth step.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x67F6C8..0x67F7BF: mov ecx,0x59F; call SaveWriteKey; call 0xA79750; walk [state+0x20] with esi=[node], next=[node+8]; the tag string at [esi+0x94]/[esi+0x98]; call 0xA78AF0 (SaveWriteNamedObject). Every one of the 33 saves has the key, 26 of them empty as `sunk_ships={ }` - the positive and negative case both. Wrong if a save without the key were found.

addresses.name: CCombatant_LoadKey_SunkShipArm
addresses.comment: **A combatant's `sunk_ship` key points into the game state's sunk list, by id.** CCombatant::LoadKey's arm for token 0x5A1: where the value is a block (atoi of its text is 0), the `{ id= type= }` pair is read (ParseObjectId) and looked up with FindPersistentByIdPair; **a ship found** is appended to the side's sunk list (+0x28 first, +0x2C last, +0x30 count), **one not found is dropped without a word**. The ship found is the CShip the top-level `sunk_ships` block made - that block precedes `combat` in a save. CCombatant::SaveContents writes the pair from the ship's own id (+0x8 type, +0xC serial) for each node, before `losses`.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x564F46..0x564FEC: atoi on parse+0x22C, jne to the default; call 0xA7B250; call 0xA9D390; je to the end on null; 0x10-byte node {ship, [edi+0x2C], 0, 0}. In CCombatant::SaveContents (0x565010) the loop at 0x56509D reads [ebx+0x28], data [esi], id [eax+8]/[eax+0xC], key 0x5A1. Checked in Ireland1937_11_02_21: the naval battle's defender has sunk_ship {4775, 41}, which is the last entry of that save's sunk_ships (CHI destroyer 'Di 2 Quzujian Dadui', sunk_by {2090, 41}). Wrong if a save held a combatant's sunk_ship id with no matching sunk_ships entry and the original kept it.

addresses.name: CCombatHistory_LoadEntries
addresses.comment: **Reads the list of finished battles back** for CCombatHistory::LoadKey's one key, `history`, with the list at the history's +8. Until `}` or the end of the file: an entry is built on the stack - its table 0x15B68C0, 0x18D, its hour (+0x8) the null date 0x29C55C0 (year 5000) from [0x170C2B8], the two country ids (+0x14, +0x1C), the convoy byte (+0x20) and the province (+0x24) nought; **the kind (+0xC) and the two tag texts (+0x10, +0x18) are not initialised** - and loaded through its slot 3 (CCombatHistoryEntry::LoadKey per key); then a 0x34-byte copy is **appended at the end** with `previous` (+0x28) the old last, `next` (+0x2C) nought and `pruned` (+0x30) nought. **Nothing is pruned, sorted or checked here** - CCombatHistory::Prune runs only from CCombatManager::Tick, so the first hour after a load is what trims the list - and nothing empties the list first: CGameState::ResetSession does not touch it (see the CCombatHistoryEntry::LoadKey comment), so entries from the session before a load stay ahead of the loaded ones until that prune. `ret 8` at 0x43428D. Was CCombatHistory_BuildEntry_A, 'almost certainly save or load'.

addresses.name: CBomberCombatant::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CBomberCombatant::LoadKey(CBomberCombatant* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **The keys its switch names**, 4 of them, one case each, and where each lands: `strength` (0x259) through TokenToFixedPoint into `strength_damage_dealt` (+0x10E4); `building` (0x1FE), `pool` (0x484) and `current_producing` (0x485) through ReadFixedVectorInPlace (rva 0x45140) into the vectors at +0x10B4, +0x10C4 and +0x10D4. **Those three are filled in place**: the constructor already sized them - one per building of the database, seven, seven - and the reader stores figure i only while i is inside that length, consuming and dropping any figure past it and leaving any it does not get at nought. So a save written under a buildings.txt of another length loads without error and silently misplaces nothing past the shorter of the two. Every other key goes to CCombatant::LoadKey (0x164DD0) - `dice`, `unit`, `sunk_ship`, `losses`, `size`, `tactic`. Not saved and so as the constructor leaves it after a load: the target list (+0xB4) and its count (+0xB0) - filled afresh for every unit in every hour by CollectFightingLandTargets / CollectBombTargets before any wing fires - and everything else CCombatant does not save.

The constructor's sizing is the record's (CBomberCombatant::CBomberCombatant, rva 0x15DBC0). Wrong if a save of the base game ever showed a `building` list of other than 12 figures - all five do not.

addresses.name: ReadFixedVectorInPlace
addresses.comment: **Reads a block of bare fixed-point numbers into an int vector that is already the right length.** Until `}` (token 4) or the end of the file (0x13): each token is taken, and while its index is below the vector's length ((end - begin) / 4) its value in thousandths is stored at that index; past the length the token is consumed and dropped. It never grows or shrinks the vector, so the length is whatever the owner's constructor gave it and figures the block does not reach keep their old value. Used for CBomberCombatant's `building`, `pool` and `current_producing` and CCombatant's `size`. `ret 8` at 0x4451F9. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x445140..0x4451F9: the token copy (0x41 dwords), cmp against 4 and 0x13, the advance through the tokenizer's slot 1, `cmp ebx, ecx; jge 0x445150` with ecx = (vector+4 - vector+0) >> 2, then 0xA696A0 into a local and the store at [begin + ebx*4]. Callers seen: 0x55FE3C, 0x55FE51, 0x55FE7E (CBomberCombatant::LoadKey), 0x564EB9 (CCombatant::LoadKey `size`). Wrong if the vector were resized anywhere in the body - there is no call that could.

The writer is in EDI from the caller (push edi before each call in CBomberCombatant::SaveContents) - so the convention is key in ECX, writer in EDI, vector on the stack: likely, and why the signature is marked inferred. struct_fields.name: is_convoy_battle
struct_fields.comment: **Set for a convoy raid's battle**: the constructor copies the combat's byte +0x2B (written by ResolveConvoyRaid) into this byte. Saved as `convoy=yes` only when set, read back as yes/no; only ever on a kind-2 entry in the saves. Read by CEU3AI_AssignSeaTargetsToAgents (kind 2, this set, a month old at most) for the AI's convoy-raid provinces. The three bytes after it are padding.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor 0x42F370: mov cl,[edi+0x2B]; mov [esi+0x20],cl - a byte. SaveContents: movzx eax, byte ptr [edi+0x20]. LoadKey: the yes/no reader 0xA697B0 with edi = esi+0x20. Was `flag int`, 'copied from the combat's byte +0x2B'; the name and type are what changes. Wrong if a dword read of +0x20 existed - none in the three bodies.

struct_fields.name: strength_damage_dealt
struct_fields.comment: **The strength damage this bombing side has dealt**, accumulated one shot at a time by FireUnit (`add [side+0x10E4], esi` at 0x16149C) - damage put on the targets before it is settled, so a little above the bombed side's `losses` (46.039 against 45.900 in Ireland1938_08_03_14). Saved as **`strength`** by CBomberCombatant::SaveContents (0x15FE90 - slot 2, which this comment used to call a getter) and read back by CBomberCombatant::LoadKey (0x15FDF0). At the end of the bombing CBomberCombatant::ReportBombingEnd (slot 10, 0x15E030) multiplies it by 10 and divides by 1000 and writes it back for its BOMB_DAMAGE_MEN line.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x55FEAA reads it for the save, 0x55FE26 stores it on load, 0x55EF74..0x55EF91 the end-of-bombing scaling. The figures are the three land bombings of Ireland1938_08_03_14. Only the comment changes.

struct_fields.name: buildings_destroyed
struct_fields.comment: An array by the building's place in the database - **index 0 the built-in `nobuilding`, then common/buildings.txt in file order**, so 12 in Their Finest Hour - of what CSubUnit::BombProvince has taken off each kind of building, in thousandths of a level, summed over the bombing. Saved as `building` (all figures, through SaveWriteFixedVector) and filled back in place by CBomberCombatant::LoadKey. In Germany1936_09_02_21's ground bombing of 2558 index 5 is 0.426 (anti_air, which stands at 0.574 of 1 in the province) and index 10 is 0.421 (industry). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 6.
struct_fields.evidence: The constructor sizes it by the database's vector; the database's entry 0 is nobuilding (the record's g_CBuildingDataBase and CProvince +0x310 comments); 11 entries in tfh/common/buildings.txt and 12 figures in every saved bomber block. Only the comment changes.

struct_fields.name: stockpile_destroyed
struct_fields.comment: Seven figures, in the goods order supplies, fuel, money, crude oil, metal, energy, rare materials: what CSubUnit::BombProvince has taken out of the province's pool over the bombing (a logistical strike's supplies and fuel). Saved as `pool` and filled back in place by CBomberCombatant::LoadKey. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 6.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor: seven pushes; SaveContents key 0x484 over +0x10C4. Only the comment changes.

struct_fields.name: production_destroyed
struct_fields.comment: Seven figures, in the goods order supplies, fuel, money, crude oil, metal, energy, rare materials: what CSubUnit::BombProvince has taken off the province's `current_producing` over the bombing (a strategic bombing's crude oil, metal, energy and rare materials). Saved as `current_producing` and filled back in place by CBomberCombatant::LoadKey. Germany1936_09_02_21's strategic bombing of 2558 holds 0 0 0 0 2.300 2.300 2.300, and the province's metal, energy and rare materials stand exactly 2.300 under their maximum. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 6.
struct_fields.evidence: SaveContents key 0x485 over +0x10D4; the province block of 2558 in the same save: current_producing metal 4.7 energy 3.7 rare 1.7 against max 7, 6, 4. Only the comment changes.

struct_fields.name: sunk_ships
struct_fields.comment: The head of the list of ships (CSubUnit*) this side has lost - CUnit::RemoveSpentSubUnits appends a ship of a fleet in a battle, CBomberCombatant::FireUnit a ship its bombs finish - with the tail at +0x2C and the count at +0x30; nodes {ship, previous, next}. **The ships themselves live on the game state's sunk list** (CGameState +0x20). CCombatant::SaveContents writes one `sunk_ship={ id= type= }` per node from the ship's own id (+0x8/+0xC), after the units and before `losses`; CCombatant::LoadKey finds each again by FindPersistentByIdPair and drops one it cannot find. CCombat::Conclude names them in the battle's message. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, sections A.3 and B.4.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x56509D..0x5650CF: [ebx+0x28], data [esi], id [eax+8]/[eax+0xC], next [esi+8]. The old comment said the key was written 'out of [node + 0xC]'; it is out of the ship the node holds. Ireland1937_11_02_21: the id written is the last sunk_ships entry's. Only the comment changes.

struct_fields.name: sunk_ships
struct_fields.comment: The head of the list of **every ship that has left the game this session** - sunk in a battle (CUnit::RemoveSpentSubUnits), sunk by bombs, disbanded alone (CDisbandRegimentCommand) or with its fleet, or taken with a unit removed for any reason (CGameState::RemoveUnit) - all through CGameState::DisposeSubUnit, which keeps a CShip here instead of deleting it; tail +0x24, count +0x28, 0x10-byte nodes {ship, previous, next, byte}. Never pruned: only CGameState::ResetSession empties it, deleting each ship. Saved as the top-level `sunk_ships` block, `<owner tag>={ship}` per node in list order, read back with each ship's owner from its key (CGameState_LoadKey_SunkShipsArm). Read by `total_of_ours_sunk` and `total_sunk_by_us`, and the ships are what combatants' `sunk_ship` ids resolve to. **Read live**: 1295 CShip in a 1942 game.
struct_fields.evidence: DisposeSubUnit (0x684CE0) appends at 0x684DDC..0x684E20; its seven callers by findRefs; ResetSession 0x67BE0F..0x67BE3E deletes and zeroes. Saves: Germany1936_03_31_19's two POL ships stand at strength 100 with no sunk_by - removed, not sunk. Only the comment changes.

Never pruned: only CGameState::ResetSession empties it, deleting each ship. Saved as the top-level `sunk_ships` block, `<owner tag>={ship}` per node in list order, read back with each ship's owner from its key (CGameState_LoadKey_SunkShipsArm). Read by `total_of_ours_sunk` and `total_sunk_by_us`, and the ships are what combatants' `sunk_ship` ids resolve to. **Read live**: 1295 CShip in a 1942 game.
